第 24 章 Like This? Really?就这样？真的吗？

Dave Mangot / 戴夫·曼戈特

— 第 73 页 —

I'd been involved in recruiting engineers for much of my career, as a team lead or a senior engineer. But it was not until I became an engineering manager that I truly became horrified by the state of affairs. At many places, when we needed to hire someone, there was a call to the recruiters, who sent tons of cold InMail's to people who might fit the role. There was a stack of potential candidates (if we were lucky) who were invited to come to the office for hours of whiteboard coding and "culture fit" interviews, until we finally settled on a person we were supposed to work with daily for many years. As an engineer at heart, I would have a difficult time thinking of a more poorly designed system. There has to be a better way.

我职业生涯的大部分时间都在招聘工程师，作为团队负责人或高级工程师。但直到我成为工程经理，我才真正对现状感到恐惧。在很多地方，当我们需要招人时，就是给招聘人员打电话，他们给可能适合的人发一堆冷 InMail。有一堆潜在候选人（如果我们幸运的话）被邀请来办公室进行几小时的白板编码和「文化匹配」面试，直到我们最终选定一个我们应该每天共事多年的人。作为一个骨子里的工程师，我很难想到一个设计更差的系统。一定有更好的方式。

The Funnel漏斗

The places where I've worked that recruited well approached the problem from an engineering perspective. What are our inputs and outputs, and how do we use our processing time most efficiently? There can be many criteria for the inputs to our funnel (yes, ultimately recruiting is a sales effort) depending on the engineer we want to attract.

我工作过的招聘做得好的地方都是从工程角度处理这个问题的。我们的输入和输出是什么？我们如何最高效地利用处理时间？根据我们想吸引的工程师，我们漏斗的输入可以有很多标准（是的，招聘最终是销售工作）。

If we want a more diverse pool, we need to make sure our organization is positioned that way by being involved with the appropriate organizations or schools and staffing and supporting our own roles to attract and retain the people we want. If we want people straight out of college, we should have an internship program with a local university. If we want Java programmers, we need to be involved in the Java community. Conferences and meetups are great for this. We want to build the relationships ahead of time, not at the very last moment when they are called for.

如果我们想要更多元的人才库，我们需要通过参与合适的组织或学校、配置和支持我们自己的岗位来吸引和留住想要的人，确保组织以那种方式定位。如果我们想要刚毕业的人，我们应该和当地大学有实习项目。如果我们想要 Java 程序员，我们需要参与 Java 社区。会议和聚会很适合这个。我们想提前建立关系，而不是在需要的最后一刻。

As they enter the funnel, we should ask what they're looking for and clearly describe what we're offering. Design the funnel intentionally and make it repeatable. As candidates move through the funnel, we should make sure that each successive interaction brings them closer to a job offer. If they have no chance of success, or new interactions won't bring them closer, we should be respectful of both our time and theirs and exit them from the process.

当他们进入漏斗时，我们应该问他们在找什么，清楚描述我们提供什么。有意识地设计漏斗，让它可重复。当候选人在漏斗中移动时，我们应该确保每次后续互动都让他们更接近 offer。如果他们没有成功机会，或者新的互动不会让他们更近，我们应该尊重双方的时间，让他们退出流程。

— 第 74 页 —

The Coding Test编码测试

If you have a coding test (and yes, if you're hiring engineers, you should), make it something real. If your existing engineers don't write their code on a whiteboard, neither should your prospective ones. Design a test that is applicable to the work they would do. Then, send it home with them. Here are some question that you should consider:

如果你有编码测试（是的，如果你招工程师，你应该有），让它是真实的。如果你的现有工程师不在白板上写代码，你的未来工程师也不该。设计一个适用于他们会做的工作的测试。然后，让他们带回家做。以下是一些你应该考虑的问题：

What if they use StackOverflow, or other similar resources?

如果他们用 StackOverflow 或类似资源怎么办？

What if they do? They're normal?

那又怎样？他们是正常人？

What if someone writes it for them?

如果有人替他们写怎么办？

You're going to ask them to explain parts of the code, in detail. Why they made decisions. How does a lambda work? If they don't understand the code, that will be very obvious.

你会让他们详细解释代码的部分内容。他们为什么做这些决定。lambda 怎么工作？如果他们不理解代码，会非常明显。

What if they cheat?

如果他们作弊怎么办？

They might. But, if you begin your relationships assuming the worst about potential employees, instead of treating them like mature adults, you probably have other things to work on in your org besides recruiting.

可能会。但是，如果你以对潜在员工做最坏假设的方式开始关系，而不是像成熟成年人一样对待他们，那你的组织除了招聘可能还有其他要改进的地方。

Closing the Deal成交

After a candidate has spent all this time with your organization and they've passed all the screening you've carefully devised, it's time to close the deal. Ultimately, recruiting is a sales job, and we need to know what we're selling. Up until this point, much of the onus of selling is on the candidate. At this point, it's on you. Like any good sales person you need to know the strengths and weaknesses of what you're selling. Above all, you need to be honest about it. Candidates can sense if you're being evasive about the fact that your CTO regularly logs into production hosts and changes configurations. You probably don't need to be forthcoming about every blemish, but you shouldn't hide from them either. Honesty is appreciated, with context.

当候选人在你的组织花了这么多时间、通过了你精心设计的所有筛选之后，就是成交的时候了。最终，招聘是销售工作，我们需要知道我们在卖什么。到目前为止，销售的责任大部分在候选人身上。这时候，在你身上。像任何好的销售人员一样，你需要知道你卖的东西的优缺点。最重要的是，你需要诚实。候选人能感觉到你是否在回避你的 CTO 经常登录生产主机改配置这个事实。你可能不需要把每个瑕疵都主动说出来，但你也不应该对他们隐瞒。带着上下文的诚实是值得赞赏的。

— 第 75 页 —

Know the advantages of your organization. Maybe you have a great mentoring program with senior staff. Maybe it's a small, scrappy organization where they could have a lot of impact. Maybe it's a large organization with lots of opportunity for career advancement and restricted stock units (RSUs). Like any good sales person, know to whom you're selling, what they want and need, and how well the product (the job) matches up.

了解你组织的优势。也许你有很好的高级员工辅导项目。也许这是一个小而精的组织，他们可以产生很大影响。也许这是一个大组织，有很多职业发展机会和限制性股票（RSU）。像任何好的销售人员一样，知道你在卖给谁、他们想要和需要什么、产品（工作）匹配得如何。

If the candidate is happy with the opportunity you present and they choose a role at your company, congratulations! Now scale it.

如果候选人对你提供的机会满意、选择了你公司的职位，恭喜！现在规模化它。
